source.title: Grokking in LLM Pretraining? Monitor Memorization-to-Generalization without Test
source.authors: Zi-Yue Li; Chenrui Fan; Tianyi Zhou

record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization during pretraining in new settings: a 7B MoE LLM and a 55M MoE model, using downstream benchmark performance and routing-pathway measurements rather than small algorithmic datasets.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own delayed downstream-performance results, pathway dynamics, and pathway–accuracy correlations. Cited results about small algorithmic grokking are not recorded as findings of this study. The correlation analysis in the main OLMoE experiments is restricted to checkpoints after domain accuracy begins a sustained rise, so it does not establish advance prediction of the initial rise.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own measurements of delayed downstream generalization after training-loss convergence during near-single-pass pretraining of a 7B MoE LLM (OLMoE) on heterogeneous text. This is a new, realistic setting for V4 and the non-algorithmic-data part of V3. It also tracks continuous internal routing-pathway measures after memorization and correlates them with benchmark accuracy, which bears partly on V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that grokking (delayed generalization after memorization) occurs in near-single-pass MoE LLM pretraining but is local and asynchronous across data groups. They argue that routing pathways become more shared and consistent after memorization, that two pathway metrics provide a zero-cost monitor of generalization, and that a one-layer MoE theory links simpler routing to a better generalization bound.
record.recipe_differences: Uses near-single-pass pretraining of an existing 7B MoE LLM on heterogeneous text, measures memorization with per-sample pretraining loss, and evaluates downstream tasks after lightweight instruction tuning; also analyzes a trained 55M MoE. This differs from small networks trained for many epochs on small algorithmic datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported grokking delays vary by domain and paired data group; pathway change varies by layer, including an increase in edit distance at the final layer. The paper reports pathway-trend robustness to routing-weight threshold and memorization thresholds ε and δ, and correlation robustness to LoRA rank 32 versus 64 on commonsense.

fits_no_version.finding: In OLMoE math pairs, groups memorized later have longer memorization-to-generalization delays; the authors attribute this to data difficulty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LLM pretraining, the grokking delay scales with the difficulty or memorization time of a data group (not with training-set size).

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), as stated in the supplied metadata
record.problems: The principal experiments use one 7B model and ten sampled checkpoints. Downstream evaluation requires instruction tuning. Paired groups are formed by embedding-based matching. The main correlation analysis is limited to checkpoints after benchmark accuracy begins a sustained rise, so it does not establish advance prediction of that rise. Several trajectory values are presented in figures without numeric values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results left out. Theoretical and synthetic routing-kernel results, parameter-update analyses, and comparisons with training or validation loss were not included because they do not directly measure the delayed downstream-generalization behavior or the pathway metrics tied to it in the tested versions.

untested.parts: Entire version: small algorithmic datasets, chance-to-near-perfect test accuracy, and delay vs training-set size.

No specific generalizing circuit is identified. Removal of memorizing components is not shown. Anticipation of the jump is not tested, because correlations use only checkpoints after the sustained accuracy rise begins.
Images and molecules; switching the delay on or off via initialization scale or weight norm (lazy-to-rich transition).
Fine-tuning on realistic data; dense (non-MoE) LLMs.

missing.what: Numeric delays annotated in Figure 2 (120k, 365k, 370k, 485k steps), absent from the row values.
LoRA rank 64 ablation: commonsense pathway correlations stay similar (distance Pearson -0.9927, consistency 0.9559).
Cross-domain (math × code) pathway edit distance shows no systematic decline, supporting that reorganization is within-domain.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T3. Main caveats: one 7B model with only ten checkpoints; memorization is defined by low, stable per-sample training loss in single-pass training; generalization is measured after LoRA instruction tuning; test groups are selected as samples that become consistently correct and paired by embedding matching, so measured delays partly reflect construction. The nanoMoE experiment gives no downstream delay result, only pathway dynamics and correlations. The original sources are not this study, so verdicts are permitted.

versions.untested_parts: Small algorithmic datasets, training accuracy versus test accuracy, chance-to-near-perfect transition, and the effect of training-set size on delay.

The paper measures gradual MoE routing-pathway changes and their relation to downstream performance, but does not identify a Fourier algorithm or other specific generalizing circuit, demonstrate removal of memorizing components, or establish that its metrics anticipate the initial accuracy rise.
Tests non-algorithmic text pretraining, but does not test images or molecules, initialization scale, weight norm, or switching a grokking-like delay on or off.
Tests pretraining, not realistic-data fine-tuning; the principal 7B-model benchmark evaluation uses lightweight instruction tuning after checkpoints are taken.
Does not test weight decay or another low-norm bias, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
Does not test whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities, floating-point softmax limits, or whether controlling them removes the delay.
